title: Severity-gated remediation of all 72 deep-EM findings
summary: Stabilize durability and authority in H1, execute pairwise-disjoint H2 and H3 lanes with low companions, enforce an independent exact-SHA high closure gate, then execute concurrent M1 and M2 lanes with the remaining low companions before one final integration and full-suite evaluation.

current_state.summary: At reviewed SHA 00cd4f2c8183e57b6eae3f0cb6b0c580e00fe085, Taskplane is a stdlib-first Python plugin with file-backed governance, immutable/CAS evidence primitives, a server-rendered dashboard, graph/review subsystems, CI, packaging, and repository documentation. The deep EM review found 72 open obligations: several durability and authority abstractions exist but are incompletely composed or ordered; multiple production validators are unwired; review/preview/repository work has unbounded paths; the dashboard and graph overstate interaction/state semantics; privacy and compatibility claims diverge from behavior; CI lacks reproducible Python quality controls; and global test/runtime seams are not isolated.

alternatives.name: Contract-first severity train
alternatives.description: Stabilize shared durability, authority, compatibility, and timeout contracts in H1; fan out H2/H3 and then M1/M2 by exclusive file/interface owner; join each branch; enforce an independent high gate; finish with one exact-SHA integration evaluation.

gains: Preserves the high-first Product priority and fail-closed medium eligibility
Maximizes safe native parallelism without duplicate file or interface ownership
Reuses incumbent modules and introduces only three acceptance-traceable support modules
costs: Broad modules such as dashboard.py and taskplane_lite.py require one owner per wave
The exact 72-row map and gate add deliberate validation overhead
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Two consecutive releases show the same broad-file owner is still the dominant critical-path bottleneck after this remediation.

alternatives.name: Lens-owned remediation train
alternatives.description: Assign one Build task to each of the 26 review lenses and integrate lens results in severity order.

costs: Creates concurrent ownership conflicts in dashboard.py, taskplane_lite.py, CI, docs, and shared contracts
Duplicates root fixes for corroborating findings
Lens order does not express implementation dependencies
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A future canonical review includes a proven file/interface ownership partition instead of lens ownership.

alternatives.name: Monolithic remediation branch
alternatives.description: Fix all 72 findings in one task and validate only after the entire change is complete.

costs: High closure waits behind documentation and low-risk changes
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A future remediation inventory is local, reversible, and has one root cause.

alternatives.name: High-only correction with medium/low deferral
alternatives.description: Close the 34 high findings and convert medium/low findings into backlog.

costs: Contradicts R-0002 and explicit human scope
Leaves known production, privacy, quality, and documentation defects
Creates the forbidden low-only tail or silent deferral
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Only after a new attributed Product scope decision.

decision: Select contract-first-severity-train. H1 is the only prerequisite foundation. After H1-I, H2 and H3 use exclusive owners and may execute together; where a graph file serves both branches, one named HX-GRAPH owner carries both obligations. HG-EVAL independently closes exactly 34 highs at one SHA. Only then do M1 and M2 execute, with MX-DOCS-ARCH owning the one cross-branch documentation/architecture surface. All low findings are attached to their earliest related owner and never form a tail. Taskplane emits dependency/scope intent only; Codex native subagents own dispatch, lifecycle, concurrency, and one event-driven wait per ready set.

contracts.description: One immutable finding map, enforceable code-quality and boundedness rules, production reachability, deterministic tests, and exact closure evidence.
Prepare/durable-commit ordering, exclusive successors, restart recovery, non-authoritative partial migration, and root authority.
Supported composition roots and bounded live entry points for reviewed validators, previews, review, and repository operations.
Keyboard/ARIA semantics, truthful asynchronous and fallback actions, honest states, reduced motion, contrast, and accessible text.
Sanitized durable commands/audit, bounded raw diffs, minimized shared metadata, safe defaults, and accurate disclosures.
Current and last-released compatibility, explicit packaging authority, and exact-SHA immutable terminal evidence.
Hash-locked CI dependencies, least checkout privilege, lint, strict typing, mandatory proofs, and dev-only assets.
Independent fail-closed eligibility for medium work after exactly 34 high results close at one SHA.
Locale/plural formatting, deterministic fallback, grapheme-safe visible truncation, and full accessible text.
Context-scoped nested and concurrent-safe dependency bindings with deterministic restoration.
Generated CLI/help/navigation/onboarding content remains aligned with supported behavior.
Focused, integration, high-gate, and final results bound to one exact clean candidate SHA.

native_execution.taskplane_authority: dependency classification, scoped contract emission, evidence validation, and orchestrator gates only
native_execution.ready_set_rule: Dispatch every ready pairwise-disjoint lane concurrently with exact emitted identities.
native_execution.wait_rule: Issue one event-driven wait for the full outstanding ready set; reissue only after completion or attributed attention, never on a schedule.
native_execution.overlap_rule: Any shared file, fixture, schema, public contract, composition root, or integration path has one named owner or an explicit dependency before dispatch.

high_closure_gate.rule: Exactly 34 unique closed rows, one exact clean candidate SHA, passing focused selector fingerprints, independent evaluator identity distinct from Build owners, and zero missing/open/suppressed/downgraded/self-attested result.
high_closure_gate.negative_evidence: Remove, duplicate, downgrade, suppress, change SHA, or mark one row self-attested; each mutation must refuse medium eligibility.

alerts: Block H1-I on any incomplete intent, split successor, non-durable acknowledgement, or incomplete migration authority.
Block H2-I on an unwired production surface, unbounded operation, disabled limit, or missing quality gate.
Block H3-I on false action/state semantics, accessibility failure, unbounded personal data, identity leakage, or stale terminal SHA.
Block medium eligibility when HG-EVAL cardinality, independence, SHA, status, or selector integrity fails.
Block M1-I on moving dependencies, missing mandatory proof, import-time mutation, retry duplication, or unsafe binding restoration.
Block M2-I on locale/grapheme, privacy/product claim, generated-doc, navigation, onboarding, concurrency, or debt-trace mismatch.
Block completion when FINAL-EVAL finds any trace/graph drift or the single final suite fails.
observability.privacy: Persist bounded typed status, counts, ids, fingerprints, SHA, durations, and redacted error classes. Do not persist raw commands, diffs, prompts, absolute private paths, workstation identity, secrets, credentials, or free-text personal data outside the explicit private locator or bounded encrypted/local evidence policy.

rollout.strategy: Use native task branches and merge-on-green per declared owner. H1 leaf tasks run first and H1-I stabilizes versioned durable/authority contracts. H2 and H3 leaves then run concurrently with HX-GRAPH as the single shared graph owner, followed by H2-I/H3-I and independent HG-EVAL. Only after the high gate passes do M1/M2 leaves run concurrently, with MX-DOCS-ARCH as the single shared loop-design owner. FINAL-I reconciles trace, graph, compatibility, and exact-SHA surfaces; FINAL-EVAL runs all focused/applicable checks and the full suite once. No Taskplane lens workers, scheduler, polling, push, tag, release, publication, or main mutation is part of this rollout.
rollout.rollback: Before each join, discard only the failing owner branch and keep prior green contracts. Persistence changes retain dual-read/additive schemas and never make partial migration authoritative. After a terminal CAS, never rewrite immutable evidence: disable the candidate, restore the last green reader/writer path, and append a successor at a new SHA. Dashboard/docs/CI/wiring removals restore the last supported surface and its matching claims. Packaging remains ineligible without current/N-1 compatibility and explicit release authority.

steps: Readers accept current and new versioned durable/evidence shapes.
Writers emit prepared, durable, reconciled new shapes while old readers remain supported.
Crash/restart/migration fault matrices prove predecessor-or-one-successor semantics.
Current/last-released mixed matrix and production reachability selectors pass.
Only an explicitly authorized later release may retire legacy writes.
compatibility_and_migration.knowledge_store: Copy to a non-authoritative destination with manifest and content verification, fsync files/directories, write copy-complete marker, then atomically switch the private locator; interruption leaves legacy authoritative.
compatibility_and_migration.terminal_evidence: Immutable bundles and exports are append-only exact-SHA objects; stale artifacts remain historical and cannot be rewritten into current authority.

python_design.execution_model: Synchronous ownership by default; existing asynchronous host/event paths must propagate cancellation and surface pending/success/failure without unowned background tasks.
python_design.shared_state: Protect cross-thread/process state with locks, immutable values, and context-local bindings; do not rely on the GIL, and run concurrent restoration/CAS tests compatible with free-threaded execution.
python_design.packaging: Runtime remains stdlib-only. Development dependencies are hash-locked separately; Pillow is development/asset-generation only. Verify clean-wheel installation, public import surface, package resources, Python floor, and import graph.

visualization.reason: The high-first gate, two concurrent branch pairs, cross-branch shared owners, and low-companion placement are material execution decisions that prose alone makes difficult to verify.

references_applied.application: Checked as-built grounding, real alternatives, numeric quality targets, executable acceptance mapping, signal-linked failures, additive rollback, proportional modules, buildable ownership, terminology, and honest self-attestation.

Specified synchronous/async ownership, cancellation, consuming-boundary protocols, trust-boundary validation, no import-time service locators, Python packaging/dependency policy, free-threaded shared-state controls, strict types, clean-wheel, and graph verification.

lens_evidence.evidence: Grounded the design in exact reviewed sources and graph; compared four material approaches; mapped 8 acceptance criteria and all 72 findings to modules/contracts, exclusive owners, dependencies, and executable selectors; set numeric durability/budget/timeout/accessibility/Python targets; linked every failure detection to an observability signal and bounded recovery; preserved current/N-1 expand-contract rollback; limited new modules to traceability, neutral glob matching, and locale/text boundaries; and left no implementation decision open.
